implementation.ownership: Private root holds canonical text. Worker fields reconstruct a private canonical root; reads/results/notifications stay detached. Synchronous callbacks receive no private borrowed cache.
implementation.transfer: One lazy worker, one active encoder job. Reuse its last baseline for changed-field messages; reseed after mismatch, synchronous publication, failed candidates or thread retirement.
implementation.lifecycle: Default 30-second job deadline and 60-second idle retirement. Active jobs retain the thread until result or actual exit; normal app shutdown flushes before disposal, forced shutdown requests termination.
implementation.memoryPolicy: Production maxBytes defaults to Infinity and does not impose a new settings-file size limit. Configurable limits are tested only on independent encoder instances. This is not a bound on total settings memory.
implementation.compatibility: JSON file, atomic replace and queue remain. Desktop settings responses remain complete; only explicit returnSettings:false omits a snapshot, used by phone HTTP media services. Custom serializers keep their property key.

limitations: Three alternating local samples are not P95 or sustained playback/query/thumbnail responsiveness acceptance. One no-op listener excludes actual renderer/IPC preparation.

Only main-thread JSON calls are counted. Worker still stringifies/parses; main still parses snapshots and clones changed payloads for postMessage. Ordinary writes have two main parses, not zero copies.
Whole-tag total median did not improve (70.0195 to 71.4189 ms), and read-only did not improve (19.1318 to 19.431 ms).

Process RSS including threads increased: median before operations 80.5546875 to 97.7109375 MiB, after operations 105.80078125 to 140.96875 MiB. These are point observations affected by allocation/GC, not peaks, fixed per-thread cost, mobile PSS or long-term stability.
Earlier parallel observations, the initial baseline and the later command sample remain separately retained; source digests for earlier checkpoints are intentionally historical.
The media diagnostic is a different workload and includes prior identity/path changes; it cannot establish this batch alone caused all its improvement.

Explicit paths, custom serializers, synchronous saves, first load/extension registration and emergency synchronous exit may still serialize on the main thread. Reads/broadcast/renderer preparation and logical store separation remain work.
Atomic replacement and recovery tests do not establish fsync/power-loss durability or cross-file crash recovery.
R6 physical decoding/contention/rotation/PSS, remaining R7 startup/type/feature/UI work and R8 dependencies/migrations/signing/update/TLS remain incomplete.
